newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria parliament holds last session before poll.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria parliament holds last session before poll.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament met on Wednesday for its last session before elections in April, to discuss changes to the electoral law and a bill allowing an interim cabinet to negotiate vital loans.

Authorising the caretaker cabinet to negotiate with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will pave the way for talks on new aid to accompany a strict fixed exchange rate regime to shore up the collapsing economy.
Parliament must complete its eight-item agenda by Thursday midday, and will then be dissolved by President Petar Stoyanov, who is expected to name the caretaker cabinet later on Wednesday.
Expansion of the powers of the interim government to allow it to conclude loan agreements with other governments or lending institutions is the last item on the agenda.
After initial resistance, the majority Socialists agreed on Tuesday to support the move.

"We have tried to convince our colleagues to support the expansion of the powers of the interim government. We hope they will support it for the common good of Bulgaria," Socialist deputy Nikola Koichev, head of parliament's budget committee, told Reuters.
"There may be eventual objections as to whether this does not contradict some articles in the constitution, and there may be a debate on this."
After 30 days of mass protests, the Socialists last week gave up efforts to form a new cabinet and agreed to elections in April, 20 months before the end of their parliamentary mandate.
On Tuesday, leaders of the five parties in parliament signed a "Declaration on the Principles of Emergence from the Crisis", saying it showed unprecedented political consensus.

They agreed the caretaker cabinet must speed up long-delayed structural reforms such as privatisation and closing loss-making state firms, cutting state spending, cracking down on corruption and the grey economy, and encouraging investment.
The IMF has said it is ready to send a mission to Sofia as soon as a new government is in place, and Stoyanov has asked for aid to stabilise the economy before introduction of a currency board.
The currency board mechanism requires levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely limiting the powers of the government and the central bank.
Central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Tuesday that it could be introduced in June.

"Stabilisation measures, which may include a fixed exchange rate, can be introduced before the implementation of the currency board, if the needed financial resources for this are available," Filipov told reporters.
On the electoral law, the Socialists support lowering the limit for parties to enter parliament from its present four percent of votes.
Parliament's agenda also includes amendments to the income tax law to take account of hyper-inflation, and amendments to the state budget to allow stopgap financing for agriculture.
